This man Jeconiah is despised and scorned, like a vessel that has no use. For this reason he and his descendants have been carried away and thrown into a land they do not know.
Land, land, land, hear the word of the Lord!
This is what the Lord says: Record this man as declared childless, for among the men of his time no man from his descendants will succeed in sitting on David’s throne and ruling again in Judah.
Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture, says the Lord!

Therefore this is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says about the shepherds who tend my people: You have scattered my sheep and led them astray, and you have not cared for them. Look, I will call you to account for your evil deeds, says the Lord.
I myself will gather the remnant of my sheep from all the places where I scattered them, and I will bring them back to their fold. They will be fruitful and multiply.
I will appoint shepherds over them who will tend them. They will no longer be afraid, be scattered, or go astray, says the Lord.
Look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will raise up a righteous Branch for David. He will reign as king and act wisely, and he will establish justice and righteousness in the land.
In his days Judah will be saved, and Israel will live in peace. This is the name by which they will call him: “The Lord has vindicated us.”
Therefore, look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when people will no longer say, “As the Lord lives, who brought the house of Israel up from the land of Egypt.”

But rather, “As the Lord lives, who will bring the house of Israel up and lead them out of the northern land and out of all the places where they were scattered.” And they will live in their own land.
Concerning the prophets: My heart is broken within me, and all my bones tremble. I have become like a drunken man, like a man overcome by wine, because of the Lord and because of his holy words.

For the land is filled with adulterers and robbers. Because of these things the land mourns, and the pastures of the wilderness have dried up. Their course is evil, and they have not used their strength rightly.
For both prophets and priests have become godless. Even in my own house I have found their wickedness, says the Lord.
Therefore their paths will become slippery for them. They will be driven into darkness and fall on those paths, for I will bring disaster upon them in the year of their punishment, says the Lord.
Among the prophets of Samaria I saw falsehood: they prophesied by Baal and led my people Israel astray.

Among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen folly: they commit adultery, live by lies, and strengthen the hands of their friends [?], so that no one turns back from his evil way. They have all become like Sodom to me, and Jerusalem's inhabitants like Gomorrah.

Therefore this is what the LORD of hosts says about the prophets: Look, I will feed them bitter plants and give them bitter water to drink, because godlessness has spread from the prophets of Jerusalem throughout the land.

This is what the LORD of hosts says: Do not listen to the words of the false prophets who prophesy to you and lead you astray. They speak visions from their own hearts, not from the mouth of the LORD.
They say to those who are angry at the LORD's word, 'You will have peace.' And to everyone who follows the desires of his own heart, they say, 'No harm will come upon you.'
For who has stood in the LORD's council, seen him, and heard his word? Or who has paid attention to his word and heard it?
Look, the LORD's punishment has gone out in anger, and a blazing punishment will settle on the heads of the wicked.
The fury of the LORD's anger will not turn back until he has passed through and carried out the purpose of his heart. In the last days you will understand it.
I did not send the prophets, yet they went. I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.
They did not stand in my council, make my people hear my words, or turn them back from their evil ways and their wicked deeds.
Am I a God who is near, says the LORD, and not a God who is far away?
“If someone hides in a hiding place, do I not see him?” says the Lord. “Look, heaven and earth are full of me,” says the Lord Almighty.
I have heard what the prophets have said, prophesying lies in my name and saying, 'I dreamed a dream.'
How long will false prophecies remain in the mouths of the false prophets—prophecies from the deceit of their own hearts?
They plan to mislead my people about my name through their dreams, which they tell one another, just as their ancestors forgot my name and served Baal.
Let the prophet who has seen a dream tell the dream, and let the one who has my words speak my words truthfully. Why do you mix straw with grain? says the LORD.
Look, my words go out like fire, says the LORD, and like an iron tool that cuts stone.
Therefore, look, I am against the prophets, says the LORD, who steal my words from one another.
Look, I am against the prophets, says the LORD, who twist their tongues and say, 'This is what the LORD says.'

Look, I am against the prophets who see false dreams, says the LORD, and tell them, leading my people astray by their lies and their recklessness. I did not send them or command them, and they bring no benefit at all to this people.
When this people, or a prophet, or a priest asks you, 'What is the LORD's message?' tell them, 'This is the LORD's message: I will uproot you, says the LORD.'
As for the prophet, priest, or anyone among the people who says, 'The LORD's message,' I will punish that person and his household.
This is what each of you should say to his neighbor and to his brother: 'What has the LORD answered?' and 'What has the LORD said?'
You must no longer mention 'the LORD's message,' for the message will be each person's own prophecy. You are twisting the words of the living God, the mighty LORD, our God.
This is what you should say to a person: 'What has the LORD answered you?' and 'What has the LORD said?'
But if you say, 'The LORD's message,' this is what the LORD says: Because you have used this expression, although I sent word to you not to say it,
therefore I will surely lift you up and cast you away from my presence, together with the city that I gave to you and your ancestors.
And I will bring everlasting disgrace upon you and everlasting shame that will not be forgotten.

The Lord showed me two baskets of figs placed before the Lord’s temple, after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken captive Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, along with the craftsmen and metalworkers from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon.
One basket contained very good figs, like early figs, and the other basket contained very bad figs, too bad to eat.
The Lord said to me, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” I said, “Figs. The good ones are very good, and the bad ones are very bad, too bad to eat.”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: “Like these good figs, so I will regard with favor the exiles of Judah whom I sent from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.
I will set my eyes on them for their good, and I will bring them back to this place. I will build them up and not tear them down; I will plant them and not uproot them.
I will give them a heart to know me, that I am the Lord. They will be my people, and I will be their God, when they return to me with all their heart.

But like the bad figs that are too bad to eat—this is what the Lord says—so I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, the rest of the people who remain in this city, and those who live in the land of Egypt.
I will give them over to terror, wandering, and disaster among all the kingdoms of the earth, to disgrace, to becoming a proverb, a taunt, and a curse in all the places where I scatter them.
I will send sword, famine, and plague after them until I have wiped them out from the land that I gave to them and their ancestors.”
The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, which was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
Jeremiah the prophet spoke it concerning all the people of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying:

“From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until this day—these twenty-three years—the word of the Lord has come to me. I have spoken to you, rising early every day and speaking, but you have not listened.
The Lord sent all his servants the prophets to you, rising early and sending them, but you did not listen or turn your ears to hear.
They said, ‘Turn back, each of you, from your evil way and from your evil deeds, and live in the land that the Lord gave to you and your ancestors from long ago and forever.
Do not follow other gods to serve them and bow down to them. Do not provoke me to anger with the work of your hands, so that I will not harm you.’
But you did not listen to me, says the Lord, and you provoked me to anger with the work of your hands, bringing harm upon yourselves.
Therefore this is what the Lord of hosts says: ‘Because you have not listened to my words,

“Look, I will send for and bring all the clans of the northern kingdoms,” says the Lord, “and Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant. I will bring them against this land, its inhabitants, and all these surrounding nations. I will destroy them and make them an object of horror and hissing, and a ruin forever.”
I will make the sound of rejoicing and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstone and the light of the lamp disappear from among them.
This whole land will become a ruin and a horror, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.
When seventy years are completed, I will punish the king of Babylon and his people for their sins, says the Lord, and the land of the Chaldeans, and I will make it a horror forever.
I will bring upon that land all the words I have spoken against it, everything written in this book that Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
For many nations and great kings will enslave them too, and I will repay them according to their deeds and the work of their hands.’
For this is what the mighty Lord, the God of Israel, says: “Take from my hand this cup of the wine of wrath, and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.
They will drink and stagger and go mad because of the sword that I am sending among them.”
So I took the cup from the Lord’s hand and made all the nations to whom the Lord sent me drink.
Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, its kings and its officials, to make them a ruin and an object of horror and hissing, as they are to this day.
To Pharaoh king of Egypt, to all his servants, to his officials, and to all his people;
and to all his territories, to all the kings of the land of Uz, to all the kings of the land of the Philistines, to Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
and to Edom, Moab, and the Ammonites;
and to all the kings of Tyre, to all the kings of Sidon, and to the kings of the islands across the sea;
and to Daran [?], Teman, Buz, and all those who clip the edges of their hair;
and to all the kings whose territories border one another, and to all the kings of the Arabs who live in the wilderness;
and to all the kings of Zimran, to all the kings of Elam, and to all the kings of Media;
and to all the kings of the north, far and near, one after another, and to all the kingdoms on the face of the whole earth. And the Arsacid king will drink after them.
Say to them, “This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Drink, get drunk, stagger, and fall, never to rise again, because of the sword that I am sending among you.”
If they refuse to take the cup from your hand and drink, say to them, “This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: You must certainly drink!

For look, I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that bears my name. Will you go entirely unpunished? You will not go unpunished, because I am summoning a sword against all the inhabitants of the earth, declares the Lord Almighty.”

You must prophesy all these words against them and say to them, “The Lord will roar from on high and raise his voice from his holy dwelling. He will roar mightily over his fold. ‘Hey! Hey!’ Like someone treading grapes, he will shout against all the inhabitants of the earth.
The uproar has reached the ends of the earth, for the Lord has a case against the nations. He is judging all humanity; he has handed the wicked over to the sword, declares the Lord.
This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Look, disaster is spreading from nation to nation, and a great storm will rise from the ends of the earth.

On that day, those slain by the Lord will lie from one end of the earth to the other. No one will wail, perform mourning dances, or weep over them. They will not be gathered up or buried, but will be like dung on the ground.
Wail, shepherds, and cry out! Wallow, you mighty ones of the flock! For your days have come for slaughter. You will be shattered and fall like precious vessels.
The shepherds will have nowhere to flee, and the rams of the flock will have no escape.
The sound of the shepherds’ cries and the wailing of the rams of the flock! For the Lord has devastated their pastures.
The peaceful folds will be shattered before the Lord’s fierce anger.
For he has left his fold like a lion leaving its lair. Their land has become a wasteland because of the Lord’s anger and because of his fierce wrath.”
At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord:

“This is what the Lord says: Stand in the courtyard of the Lord’s house and speak to all the towns of Judah that come to worship in the Lord’s house. Tell them everything I commanded you to say to them. Do not leave out even one word.
Perhaps they will listen and each turn from their evil way, and I will refrain from bringing the disaster I intended to bring on them because of their evil deeds.
Say to them, ‘This is what the Lord says: Unless you listen to me and follow my law, which I have set before you,
and listen to the words of my servants the prophets, whom I send to you—I have risen early every day and sent them, but you have not listened—
I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse for all the nations of the earth.
The priests, the false prophets, and all the people heard the prophet Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the Lord.
When Jeremiah had finished saying everything the Lord had commanded him to say to all the people, the priests, the false prophets, and all the people seized him and said, “Let him be put to death,

because he prophesied in the Lord’s name and said, ‘This house will become like Shiloh, and this city will be destroyed, with no one living in it.’” All the people gathered against Jeremiah in the house of the Lord.
The officials of Judah heard these words and went up from the king’s palace to the house of the Lord. They sat at the entrance of the New Gate of the Lord’s house.

The priests and the false prophets said to the officials and all the people, “This man deserves a death sentence, because he has prophesied against this city and its inhabitants, as you have heard with your own ears.”
Jeremiah said to all the officials and all the people, “The Lord sent me to prophesy against this house and this city all the words you have heard.
Now put your ways and deeds right, and obey the Lord your God. Then the Lord will relent from the disaster he has announced against you.
As for me, here I am in your hands. Do to me whatever seems good and right to you.

But know for certain that if you kill me, you will bring the guilt of innocent blood upon yourselves, this city, and its inhabitants, because the Lord truly sent me to you to speak all these words in your hearing.”
The officials and all the people said to the priests and the false prophets, “This man does not deserve death, because he has spoken to us in the name of the Lord our God.”
Some of the elders of the land stood up and said to the whole assembly of the people,

“Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. He said to all the people of Judah, ‘This is what the Lord of hosts says: Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a ruin, and the mountain of the temple will become a wooded place.’

“Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Instead, they feared the Lord and prayed before him, and the Lord relented from the disaster he had announced against them. But we are seeking to bring great harm upon ourselves.”
There was also a man who prophesied in the name of the Lord, Uriah son of Shemaiah, from Kiriath-[?]. He prophesied against this city and this land in words like all those of Jeremiah.
King Jehoiakim, all his servants, and all his officials heard his words, and the king sought to kill him. When Uriah heard about it, he was afraid and fled to Egypt.
King Jehoiakim sent Egyptian men—Elnathan son of Achbor and some men with him—to Egypt.
They brought Uriah out of Egypt and took him to King Jehoiakim, who killed him with the sword and threw his corpse onto the graves of the common people.
But Ahikam son of Shaphan protected Jeremiah, so that he was not handed over to the people to be killed.
At the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord:
This is what the Lord said to me: “Make yourself a yoke and neckbands, and put them on your neck.
Send them to the king of Edom, the king of Moab, the king of the Ammonites, the king of Tyre, and the king of Sidon through the messengers who come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.
Command them to tell their masters: ‘This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: This is what you must tell your masters:
I made the earth, the human beings, and the animals on the face of the earth by my great power and my uplifted arm, and I give it to whomever I please.
Now I have given all these lands to serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and they will serve him. I have also given him the wild animals to serve him.
The nations will serve him, his son, and his grandson, until the time comes for his own land as well. Then many nations and great kings will make him serve them.

Any nation or kingdom that will not serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and anyone who will not put his neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon—I will punish that nation with sword, famine, and plague, declares the Lord, until I have delivered them into his hand.
Do not listen to your false prophets, your diviners, your dreamers, your omen readers, or your sorcerers, who tell you, “Do not serve the king of Babylon.”
For they are prophesying lies to you, so that I will drive you far from your land, so that I will drive you away and you will perish.
But the nation that puts its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, he will leave in its own land, says the Lord, and it will cultivate it and live in it.
I spoke to Zedekiah king of Judah in accordance with all these words. I said, “Put your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, serve him and his people, and live.
Do not die, you and your people, by sword, famine, and plague, as the Lord has said concerning the nation that will not serve the king of Babylon.
Do not listen to the words of the false prophets who tell you, ‘Do not serve the king of Babylon,’ for they are prophesying lies to you.
I did not send them, says the Lord, but they prophesy falsely in my name, so that I will drive you away and you will perish, both you and the prophets who prophesy to you.”

And to the priests and all these people, thus says the Lord: “Do not listen to the words of your prophets who prophesy to you, saying, ‘Look, the vessels of the Lord’s house will soon return from Babylon,’ for they are prophesying lies to you.
Do not listen to them, says the Lord. Serve the king of Babylon and live, so that this city will not become a ruin.

If they are prophets and the word of the Lord is in them, let them plead with the Lord Almighty that the vessels remaining in the Lord’s house, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem will not go to Babylon.
For this is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says about the pillars, the Sea, the basins, and the rest of the vessels that remain in this city:

These are the ones that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, captive from Jerusalem to Babylon, together with all the officials of Judah and Jerusalem.
Thus says the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, concerning the vessels remaining in the Lord’s house, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem:
They will go to Babylon and remain there until the day when I attend to them, says the Lord. Then I will bring them up and return them to this place.”

In that same year, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, Hananiah son of Azzur, the false prophet from Gibeon, spoke to me in the Lord’s house, in the presence of the priests and all the people:
“Thus says the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel: I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within two years I will bring back to this place all the vessels of the Lord’s house that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from this place and carried to Babylon.
Along with Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, I will bring back to this place all the exiles of Judah who went to Babylon, says the Lord, for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.”
Then Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Hananiah the false prophet in the presence of the priests and all the people standing in the Lord’s house.
Jeremiah said, “Amen! May the Lord do so! May the Lord fulfill the words you have prophesied, bringing back the vessels of the Lord’s house and all the exiles from Babylon to this place.
But listen to this word that I speak before you and before all these people.
The prophets who were before me and before you from ancient times prophesied against many lands and great kingdoms concerning war, disaster, and plague.
As for the prophet who prophesies peace, when that prophet’s word comes true, that prophet is known to have truly been sent by the Lord.”
Then Hananiah the false prophet took the yoke bars from the neck of Jeremiah the prophet and broke them.

Hananiah said in the presence of all the people, “Thus says the Lord: In this same way, within two years I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all the nations.” Then Jeremiah the prophet went on his way.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet after Hananiah the false prophet had broken the yoke bars from the neck of Jeremiah the prophet.
Go and tell Hananiah the false prophet: This is what the LORD says: In place of the wooden yokes you broke, make an iron yoke.

For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I have placed an iron yoke on the necks of all these nations so that they will serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they will serve him. I have even given him the wild animals to serve him.
Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the false prophet, “Listen, Hananiah! The LORD has not sent you, and you have made this people trust in a lie.”
Therefore this is what the LORD says: Look, I am casting you off the face of the earth. This year you will die, because you have spoken wickedness before the LORD.
Hananiah the false prophet died that year, in the seventh month.

These are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to Babylon, to the remaining elders of the exiles, to the priests, to the false prophets, and to all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken captive from Jerusalem to Babylon.
This was after King Jeconiah, the queen, the eunuchs, the officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the metalworkers had left Jerusalem.
By the hand of Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in Babylon.
This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says to all the captives who were taken from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Build houses and live in them. Plant gardens and eat their fruit.
Marry wives and have sons and daughters. Find wives for your sons, and give your daughters in marriage, so that they may have sons and daughters. Increase in number there, and do not decrease.
Seek the peace of the city where I have taken you captive, and pray to the LORD for it, for in its peace you will have peace.
For this is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Do not let the prophets among you or your diviners mislead you, and do not listen to the dreams you dream.
For they prophesy lies to you in my name, and I have not sent them, says the LORD.
For this is what the LORD says: When seventy years have been completed for Babylon, I will deliver you and fulfill my good promises to you by bringing you back to this place.
For I know the plans I am making for you, says the LORD, plans for peace and not for harm, to give you hope in the end.
You will call on me and pray before me.
And when you seek me with all your heart,

you will find me, says the LORD. I will bring back your captives and gather you from all the nations and all the lands where I have scattered you, says the LORD. I will bring you back to the place from which I took you captive.
Because you have said, “The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon,”
for this is what the LORD says about the king who sits on David’s throne and about all the people who live in this city, your fellow Israelites who did not go into captivity with you:
This is what the LORD Almighty says: Look, I am sending sword, famine, and plague against them. I will make them like bad figs that are too rotten to eat.

I will pursue them with sword, famine, and plague. I will make them an object of terror to all the kingdoms of the earth, an object of horror, cursing, reproach, and hissing among all the nations where I have scattered them.
This is because they did not listen to my words. I sent all my servants the prophets to them, sending them early, but they did not listen to them, says the LORD.
But you, all the exiles who were taken captive from Jerusalem to Babylon, listen to the word of the LORD.

This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who prophesy lies to you in my name: Look, I am handing them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will kill them with the sword before your eyes.
All the exiles of Judah in Babylon will use them in a curse, saying, “May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire.”

This is because they committed wickedness in Israel, committed adultery with their neighbors’ wives, and spoke lying words in my name that I had not commanded them to speak. I know, and I am a witness, says the LORD.
And Shemaiah the Nehelamite said:
“This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says.” And he sent a letter in his name to all the people in Jerusalem, to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to the priests:

“The Lord has appointed you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be an overseer in the Lord’s house over anyone who acts madly and prophesies falsely, so that you may put him in prison and confinement.
Now why do you not rebuke Jeremiah from Anathoth, who prophesies to you?
For he has sent word to us in Babylon: ‘You will be there a long time. Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their fruit.’”
Zephaniah the priest read this letter aloud to Jeremiah the prophet.
Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
“Send word to all the exiles: This is what the Lord says concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you although I did not send him, and has made you trust in a lie,

therefore this is what the Lord says: I am about to punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. He will have no one living among this people, nor will he see the good that I will do for my people, says the Lord, because he has spoken wickedly against the Lord.”
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
“This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Write in a book all the words I have spoken to you.

For the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will bring back the captives of my people Israel and Judah, says the Lord. I will bring them back to the land that I gave their ancestors, and they will possess it.”
These are the words that the Lord spoke concerning Israel and Judah:
“This is what the Lord says: We have heard a cry of trembling, of fear, and there is no peace.
Ask and see whether a male gives birth. Why, then, have I seen every man with his hands on his sides like a woman giving birth, and every face turned fiery?
Alas! That day is great, and there is none like it. It is a time of distress for Jacob, but he will be saved from it.
On that day, says the Lord of hosts, I will break his yoke from your neck and tear apart your bonds. Foreigners will no longer enslave them.
Instead, they will serve the Lord their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.

But you, my servant Jacob, do not be afraid, says the Lord; do not be dismayed, Israel. For I will save you from far away, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be at peace, quiet and at rest, with no one to terrify him. And you, my servant Jacob, do not be afraid, says the Lord.

For I am with you to save you, says the Lord. Though I make a complete end of all the nations among whom I scattered you, I will not make a complete end of you. I will discipline you justly, but I will certainly not leave you unpunished.
For this is what the LORD says: Your injury is painful, and your wound is severe.
There is no one to plead your case, to help you and heal you.

All your lovers have forgotten you, and they seek your life. For I have struck you as an enemy strikes, with severe discipline, because your offenses have multiplied and your sins have grown great, and you would not repent.
Why do you wail over your brokenness? Your pain is painful. Because your offenses are so many and your sins have grown great, I have done these things to you.
Therefore all who devour you will be devoured, and all your enemies will go into captivity. Those who trample you will be trampled, and all who plunder you I will give over to plunder.
For I will bring you healing and heal your wounds, says the Lord, because they have called you an outcast: ‘This is Zion, for whom no one cares.’”

This is what the Lord says: Look, I am bringing back the captives of Jacob’s dwelling and making it as it was before. I will have compassion on his dwellings. The city will be rebuilt on its mound, and the temple will be established in its rightful place.
Thanksgiving and the sound of people singing praise will come from them. I will multiply them, and they will not become few. I will strengthen them, and they will not diminish.
Their children will be as they were before, and their congregation will be established before me. I will punish all their oppressors.
Their king will be one of their own, and their ruler will come from among them. I will bring him near, and he will approach me, because he has turned his heart toward [?], says the Lord.
You will be my people, and I will be your God.
Look, the Lord’s storm goes out in fury, and a swirling storm will settle on the heads of the wicked.
The Lord’s fierce anger will not turn back until it has passed and he has fulfilled the purpose of his heart. In the last days you will understand this.
At that time, says the Lord, I will be God to all the families of Israel, and they will be my people.
This is what the Lord says: The people who escaped the sword found mercy in the wilderness. Israel went into captivity.
The Lord appeared to me from far away and said to me, “I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you to grace.”
I will build you again, and you will be rebuilt, virgin Israel. Again you will adorn yourself with ornaments and go out with the gathering of those who sing praises.
Again you will plant a vineyard on the mountain of Samaria. Plant your plants and sing praise!
For the day is coming when watchmen will call on the mountain of Ephraim and say, “Get up! Let us go up to Zion, to the Lord our God.”

For this is what the Lord says: Sing praises joyfully, people of Jacob’s house, and rejoice at the head of the nations. Proclaim, sing praise, and say, “Lord, save your people, the remnant of Israel!”

Look, I am bringing them from the northern land and gathering them from the ends of the earth, including the blind and the lame among them, pregnant women and women giving birth, all together. A great assembly will return here.

They will go with weeping and come with pleading. I will lead them beside streams of water, on straight paths where they will not stumble. For I have become a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
Hear the word of the Lord, his people, and proclaim it in the distant islands. Say, “The one who scattered Israel will gather him and guard him as a shepherd guards his flock.”
For the Lord has redeemed Jacob his servant and rescued him from the hands of one stronger than he.

They will come and sing praise on the heights of Zion. They will delight in the Lord’s good gifts: grain, wine, oil, and the young of the flocks and herds. Their lives will be like a watered garden, and they will never waste away again.
Then the virgin will rejoice with gladness, and young men and old men will rejoice together. I will turn their mourning into joy, comfort them, and give them joy instead of their sorrow.
I will satisfy the priests with rich food, and my people will be filled with my goodness, says the Lord.
This is what the Lord says: A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping. Rachel is weeping for her children and refuses to be comforted, because they are no more.
This is what the Lord says: Keep your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your tears, says the Lord. They will return from the land of their enemies.
There is hope for your future, says the Lord, and the children will return to their own territory.
I have indeed heard Ephraim lamenting and saying: You disciplined me, LORD, and I was disciplined. I was like an untamed calf. Bring me back, and I will return, for you are the LORD my God.
For after I returned, I was comforted, and after I understood, I sighed. I was ashamed and humiliated, because I bore the disgrace of my youth.
Ephraim is a precious son to me, a beloved child. Whenever I speak of him, I remember him. Therefore my compassion goes out to him, and I will have mercy on him, says the Lord.
Set up a sign for yourself and settle in the wilderness. Set your heart on the straight road. Return, virgin Israel, says the Lord, and settle in these towns of yours.
How long will you waver, repentant daughter? For the Lord has created something new on earth: a woman will love a man.

This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: From now on they will say these words in the land of Judah and in its towns, when I bring back their captives: ‘May the Lord bless you, righteous dwelling, holy mountain.’
Judah and all its towns will dwell there together, farmers and shepherds of flocks.
For I have quenched the thirst of the thirsty soul, and I have satisfied every hungry soul.
At this I awoke and looked, and my sleep had been pleasant to me.
Look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of human beings and the seed of animals.
Just as I planned against them to uproot them, tear them down, overthrow them, destroy them, and bring disaster upon them, so I will attend to them to build and to plant, says the Lord.
In those days they will no longer say, ‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge.’
Instead, each person will die for his own sins. Everyone who eats sour grapes will have his own teeth set on edge.
Look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will establish a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

It will not be like the covenant I established with their ancestors on the day I took them by the hand and brought them out of the land of Egypt. For they broke my covenant, and I in turn rejected them, says the Lord.

Instead, this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law within them and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.

They will no longer teach one another, each his brother or his neighbor, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because they will all know me, from their youngest to their oldest, says the Lord. For I will forgive their offenses and will no longer remember their sins.

This is what the Lord says, who gives the sun for light by day and the ordered course of the moon and stars for light by night, who rebukes the sea so that its waves become still—the Lord Almighty is his name:
If these established orders pass away from before me, says the Lord, then the descendants of Israel will also cease to be a people before me for all time.

This is what the Lord says: If the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below can be explored, then I too will reject all the descendants of Israel because of everything they have done, says the Lord.
Look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when the city will be rebuilt for the Lord, from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
The measuring line will again extend straight ahead over the hill of Gareb and turn toward the hill.

The whole valley where dung and ashes are thrown, as far as the Kidron stream and as far as the corner of the Horse Gate to the east, will be holy to the Lord. It will never again be uprooted or overthrown.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
At that time the armies of the king of Babylon were besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was confined in the courtyard of the guard at the palace of the king of Judah.
Zedekiah king of Judah had imprisoned him, saying: Why do you prophesy and say, ‘This is what the LORD says: I am handing this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will conquer it’?
Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the hands of the Chaldeans, but will certainly be handed over to the king of Babylon. He will speak with him face to face and look him in the eyes.
He will take Zedekiah to Babylon, and he will remain there until the day I attend to him, says the Lord. For you will fight against the Chaldeans, but you will not prevail.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
Look, Nahamiel, the son of your uncle Shallum, is coming to you and will say, ‘Buy my field in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin, because the right of inheritance belongs to you, to buy it.’

Then Hanamel, my uncle’s son, came to me in the courtyard of the guard, according to the word of the LORD, and said to me, “Buy my field at Anathoth in the land of Benjamin, for you have the right of inheritance, and the right of redemption belongs to you. Buy it for yourself.” Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD.
So I bought the field at Anathoth from Hanamel, my uncle’s son, and weighed out the money for him: seventeen shekels of silver.
I wrote the deeds and sealed them, called witnesses to attest them, and weighed the silver on the scales.
I took the deeds of purchase, both the one sealed according to the prescribed legal requirements and the unsealed one.

I gave the deeds of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah, in the presence of Nahmael, my uncle’s son, and in the presence of the witnesses whose names were written on the deeds of purchase, and in the presence of all the Jews who were sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
I instructed Baruch in their presence, saying:

“This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Take these deeds, this sealed deed of purchase and this unsealed deed, and put them in an earthenware jar so that they may be preserved for many days.
For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Houses, fields, and vineyards will again be bought in this land.”
After I had given the deeds of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed before the LORD. I prayed before the LORD and said:
“Please, Lord GOD! You made the heavens and the earth by your great power and your uplifted arm, and nothing is hidden from you.

You show kindness to thousands of generations and repay the sins of fathers into the laps of their children after them. You are the great, mighty, and awe-inspiring God, whose name is the LORD Almighty,
whose purpose is great and whose deeds are many, whose eyes are open to all the ways of human beings, to give each person according to their ways and the fruit of their deeds.
You performed great signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, and to this day for Israel among humankind, and you have made a name for yourself, as it is today.
You brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand, an uplifted arm, and a great display.
You gave them this land, which you swore to their ancestors to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
They came and took possession of it, but they did not obey your voice or follow your law. They did not do anything you commanded them to do, so you brought all this disaster upon them.

Look, the besieging forces have come against this city to capture it. The city has been handed over to the Chaldeans who are fighting against it, because of the sword, famine, and plague. What you said has happened, and you have seen it.
Yet you, Lord GOD Almighty, said to me, ‘Buy yourself a field with silver and call witnesses to attest it,’ even though the city has been handed over to the Chaldeans.”
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying:
“I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is anything hidden from me?
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am handing this city over to the Chaldeans, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will conquer it.

The Chaldeans will come and wage war against this city. They will destroy this city and burn it with fire, along with the houses on whose roofs people offered incense to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods to provoke me to anger.
For the people of Israel and the people of Judah have done what is evil in my sight from their youth. The people of Israel provoke me to anger with the work of their hands, declares the LORD.
Because of them, my anger and fury have been against this city from the day they built it until today, so that I would remove it from my presence,

because of all the evil that the people of Israel and the people of Judah have done to provoke me to anger—they, their kings, their officials, their priests, their prophets, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
They turned their backs to me and not their faces. I taught them, rising early to teach them, but they would not listen or accept correction.
They placed their abominations in the house that bears my name and defiled it.

They built high places for Baal at Topheth, in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to burn their sons and daughters for Molech. I did not command this, nor did it enter my mind that they should commit this abomination and cause Judah to sin.
Now this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning this city, of which you say, ‘It has been handed over to the king of Babylon through sword, famine, and plague.’
Look, I am gathering them from all the lands where I scattered them in my anger, my fury, and my great wrath. I will bring them back to this place and settle them in safety.
They will be my people, and I will be their God.
I will give them one heart and one spirit, so that they may fear me all their days and that it may go well with them and with their children after them.
I will establish an everlasting covenant with them: I will not turn away from doing good to them, and I will put the fear of me in their hearts so that they will not turn away from me.
I will make them glad and do good to them. I will plant them firmly in this land with all my heart and all my soul.
This is what the LORD says: Just as I brought all this great disaster upon this people, so I am bringing upon them all the good that I promise them.
Fields will be bought in this land, of which you say, ‘It is desolate, without people or livestock, and has been handed over to the Chaldeans.’

People will buy fields with silver, write and seal deeds, and witnesses will testify, in the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem, in the towns of Judah, in the towns of the hill country, in the towns of the plains, and in the towns of the south. I will bring back their captives, says the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet a second time, while he was still confined in the courtyard of the guard, saying:
This is what the LORD says, who made you, formed you, and established you—the LORD is his name:
Call to me, and I will answer you and show you great and mighty things that you have not known.
For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning the houses of this city and the houses of the kings of Judah, which the armies tore down with the sword:

They came to fight against the Chaldeans and to fill these houses with the corpses of people whom I killed in my anger and fury. I turned my face away from this city because of all the evil they did before me.
Look, I am bringing lasting healing to it. I will heal them and reveal to them paths of peace and faithfulness.
I will bring back the captives of Judah and the captives of Israel. I will rebuild them as in former times and do good to them as at the beginning.
I will cleanse them of all the wickedness by which they sinned against me, and I will forgive all their sins by which they sinned against me and rebelled against me.

The city will bring me renown, delight, joy, and glory among all the nations of the earth. They will hear of all the good I do for them, and they will fear and tremble because of all the goodness and all the peace I provide for them.

This is what the LORD says: Again there will be heard in this place, which you say is desolate, without people or livestock—in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, which are desolate, without people, inhabitants, or livestock:

The sound of rejoicing and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voices of those who say, ‘Give thanks to the LORD Almighty, for the LORD is good and kind, and his grace endures forever,’ and who bring thank offerings to the house of the LORD. For I will bring back the captives of the land as at first, says the LORD Almighty.
This is what the LORD Almighty says: In this place, which is desolate, without people or livestock, and in all its towns, there will once again be shepherds’ dwellings and resting places for sheep.

In the towns of the hill country, in the towns of the plains, in the towns of the south, in the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem, and in the towns of Judah, sheep will once again pass under the hands of the one who counts them, says the LORD.
Look, the days are coming, says the LORD, when I will fulfill the good promises I made concerning the house of Israel and the house of Judah, says the LORD.
In those days and at that time, I will cause a righteous Branch to spring up for David. He will reign as king, act wisely, and carry out justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved, and Jerusalem will dwell in safety. This is the name by which they will call him: ‘The LORD is our righteousness.’
For this is what the LORD says: David will never lack a son to sit on the throne of the house of Israel.
The priests and Levites will never lack a man before me to offer burnt offerings, make sacrifices, and burn incense every day.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
This is what the Lord says: If you can abolish my arrangements for day and my arrangements for night, so that day and night do not come at their appointed times,
then my covenant, which I promised to David my servant, can also be abolished, so that he will have no son to reign on his throne, and so can my covenant with the priests and Levites who serve me.
Just as the host of heaven cannot be counted and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the descendants of David my servant and of the Levites who serve me.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
Have you not seen what these people are saying: 'The Lord has rejected the two families he chose'? They provoke my people to anger, so that they should no longer be a people before me.
This is what the Lord says: If my covenant with day and night did not exist, and I had not established the laws of heaven and earth,

then I would also reject the descendants of Jacob and David my servant and no longer take from his descendants a ruler over the house of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For I will bring them back from captivity and have mercy on them.

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord while Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his entire army, all the kingdoms of the earth under his rule, and all the peoples were fighting against Jerusalem and all its towns:

This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Go and tell Zedekiah king of Judah, 'This is what the Lord says: Look, I am handing this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.

You will not escape from his hands. You will certainly be captured and handed over to him. Your eyes will see the eyes of the king of Babylon, and you will speak with him face to face, and you will go to Babylon.
But hear the word of the Lord, Zedekiah king of Judah. This is what the Lord says about you: You will not die by the sword.'

Instead, you will die in peace. As they mourned for your ancestors, the former kings who came before you, so they will mourn for you. They will lament over you, ‘Alas, master!’ For I have spoken this word, says the LORD.
Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem.

The armies of the king of Babylon were fighting against Jerusalem and all the remaining towns of Judah—against Lachish and Azekah, for these were the fortified towns that remained among the towns of Judah.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to proclaim people free:
Everyone was to release his male and female slaves, Hebrew men and Hebrew women, as free people, so that no one would enslave a fellow Jew.
All the officials and all the people listened and undertook to release their male and female slaves as free people, so that they would no longer make them serve as slaves, and they set them free.
But afterward they reversed their decision, enslaved those who had been freed, and made them slaves.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: I made a covenant with your ancestors on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, saying:

'After seven years, each of you must release his fellow Hebrew who has been sold to you and has served you for six years. You must let him go free from you.' But your ancestors did not listen to me or turn their ears toward me.
Today you turned back and did what was right in my eyes by proclaiming freedom, each for his fellow, and you made a covenant before me in the house that bears my name.
But you turned back again and defiled my name. Each of you brought back his male and female slaves whom you had released to live freely, and you forced them to become your male and female slaves.

Therefore this is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: You have not obeyed me by proclaiming freedom, each for his fellow. Look, I proclaim freedom for you—to the sword, famine, and pestilence, says the Lord. I will make you an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
And I will give the men who violated my covenant, who did not keep the terms of the covenant they made before me, the calf that they cut in two and passed between its halves—
the officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the eunuchs, the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the halves of the calf.
I will hand them over to their enemies and to those who seek their lives. Their corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth.
I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials to their enemies, to those who seek their lives, and to the army of the king of Babylon that is advancing against them.

Look, I am giving the command, says the Lord, and I will bring them back to this city. They will fight against it, capture it, and burn it with fire. I will turn the towns of Judah into ruins, with no one living in them.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
Go to the family of the Rechabites and speak with them. Bring them into the house of the Lord, into one of the rooms, and give them wine to drink.
So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, son of Habazziniah, his brothers, all his sons, and the whole family of the Rechabites.

I brought them into the house of the Lord, into the room of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the prophet of God, whose room was near the officials who stayed above the room of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the gatekeeper.
I set bowls full of wine and cups before the members of the Rechabite family and said to them, “Drink some wine.”
But they said, “We do not drink wine, because our ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab commanded us, saying, ‘You and your children must never drink wine.

You must not build houses for yourselves, sow seed, or plant vineyards, nor may you own them. Instead, you must live in tents all your days, so that you may live a long time in the land where you reside.’
We have obeyed the command of our ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab in everything he commanded us: never to drink wine all our days—neither we nor our wives, our sons, or our daughters;
not to build houses to live in; and not to own vineyards, fields, or seed.
We have lived in tents and have obeyed and done everything our ancestor Jonadab commanded us.
But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against the land, we said, ‘Let us go into Jerusalem to escape the army of the Chaldeans and the army of Edom.’ So we have been living in Jerusalem.”
Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah:
This is what the Lord of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Go and say to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, “Will you not accept correction and listen to my words?” says the Lord.

The words of Jonadab son of Rechab, who commanded his children not to drink wine, have been kept. They have drunk none to this day, because they obeyed their ancestor’s command. But I have spoken to you, speaking again and again, and you have not listened.

I sent all my servants the prophets to you, sending them again and again, saying, “Turn back, each of you, from your evil way, and make your deeds good. Do not follow other gods to worship them. Then live in the land that I gave to you and your ancestors.” But you did not pay attention or listen to me.
Look, the descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab have kept the command their ancestor gave them, but these people have not listened to me.

Therefore, this is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am bringing upon Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the disaster I pronounced against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen, and I called to them and they did not answer me.

Jeremiah said to the family of the Rechabites: This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Because you have obeyed the command of your ancestor Jonadab, kept all his commands, and done everything he commanded you,
therefore, this is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Jonadab son of Rechab will never lack a man to stand before me.
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord:
Take a scroll and write on it all the words I have spoken to you about Israel, Judah, and all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you, in the days of Josiah, until today.
Perhaps the house of Judah will hear about all the disaster I am planning to bring upon them, and each will turn from his evil way, so that I may forgive their guilt and their sins.
Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote on a scroll, at Jeremiah’s dictation, all the words of the Lord that he had spoken to him.
Jeremiah instructed Baruch son of Neriah, saying to him, “I am confined and cannot enter the house of the Lord.

You go in and read from the scroll you wrote at my dictation the words of the Lord before the people in the house of the Lord on the day of fasting. Read them also before all the people of Judah who come from their towns.

Perhaps their plea will come before the Lord, and each will turn from his evil way, and the Lord will relent from the disaster he has pronounced against them. For great are the anger and wrath that the Lord has declared against this people.”
Baruch son of Neriah did everything Jeremiah the prophet had instructed him to do, reading from the scroll the words of the Lord in the house of the Lord.

In the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, all the people in Jerusalem proclaimed a fast before the Lord. Baruch read before all the people who came from the towns of Judah to Jerusalem.

Baruch the scribe read the words of the Lord that Jeremiah had spoken, in the house of the Lord, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper courtyard, at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the Lord, before all the people.
Micaiah son of Gemariah, son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the Lord from the scroll.

He went down from the king’s house to the scribe’s chamber and saw all the officials sitting there: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the officials.
Micaiah told them all the words he had heard when Baruch read the scroll aloud to the people.

All the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying to him, “Take in your hand the scroll from which you read before the people, and come.” Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
The officials said to him, “Sit down and read it before us.” So Baruch read it before them.
When they heard the words, they looked at one another in alarm and said to Baruch, “We will tell the king all these words.”
They questioned Baruch, saying to him, “Tell us how you wrote all these words at his dictation.”
Baruch said to them, “Jeremiah dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them on the scroll in ink.”
The officials said to Baruch, “Go and hide, you and Jeremiah, and let no one know where you are.”
They went to the king in the courtyard, leaving the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and reported all these words to the king.
The king sent Jehudi to bring the scroll. He took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and Jehudi read it before the king and all the officials standing before the king.
The king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month, with a fire set before him.
Whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king cut it with a scribe’s knife and threw it into the burning coals, until the entire scroll was consumed in the fire on the hearth.
Neither the king nor any of his servants were afraid or tore their clothes when they heard all these words.
Even though Elnathan, Gemariah, and Delaiah pleaded with the king not to burn the scroll in the fire, he did not listen to them.
The king ordered Jerahmeel the king’s son, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to seize Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch the scribe, but the Lord hid them.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet after the king had burned the scroll and the words that Baruch had written at Jeremiah’s dictation:
“Take another scroll and write on it all the former words that were on the scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

And say to Jehoiakim king of Judah, ‘This is what the Lord says: You burned this scroll and said, “Why did you write on it that the king of Babylon would come and destroy this land and remove both people and animals from it?”
Therefore, this is what the Lord says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on David’s throne, and his corpse will lie exposed to the heat by day and the frost by night.

I will punish him, his descendants, and his servants for their wrongdoing. I will bring on them, on all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and on the people of Judah all the disaster I pronounced against them, because they did not listen to my voice.’”

Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah, the scribe. At Jeremiah’s dictation, he wrote on it all the words that had been written in the book that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. He also added many more words like them.
King Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned in place of Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had made him king in the land of Judah.
But neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words of the Lord that he spoke through Jeremiah the prophet.
King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the priests, to Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “Pray for us before the Lord your God.”
Jeremiah was going in and out among the people, for they had not put him in prison.
Pharaoh’s army came out of Egypt. When the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the news about them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet:

“This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Tell the king of Judah, who sent you to me to inquire of me, ‘Look, Pharaoh’s army, which came out to help you, has returned to its own land, to Egypt.
The Chaldeans will return and fight against this city. They will capture it and burn it down.’
This is what the Lord says: Do not imagine and say to yourselves, ‘The Chaldeans are leaving us,’ because they are not leaving.
Even if you destroyed the entire Chaldean army fighting against you, and only wounded men remained among them, they would rise, each from his tent, and burn this city down.”
The Chaldean army withdrew from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh’s army.
Jeremiah left Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin to divide a portion there with the people.
While he was standing at the Benjamin Gate, an officer was there named Nediah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah. He seized Jeremiah the prophet and said to him, “You are deserting to the Chaldeans!”
Jeremiah said to him, “You are lying! I am not deserting to the Chaldeans.” But he would not listen to him. Neriah seized Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
The officials were angry with Jeremiah. They flogged him and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe, because they had made him chief over the prisoners.
They lowered Jeremiah through the opening of the pit into the pit, and Jeremiah remained there for many days.

King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought up. The king questioned him secretly in the palace and said to him, ‘Has a word come from the LORD?’ Jeremiah said, ‘It has.’ The king said, ‘What word has come?’ He said, ‘You will be handed over to the king of Babylon.’
Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, “How have I wronged you, your servants, or this people, that you have put me in prison?
Where are your prophets who used to prophesy to you, saying, ‘The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land’?
Now listen to me, my lord the king. Let my plea come before you: do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, or I will die there.”

King Zedekiah gave orders, and they left Jeremiah the prophet in the courtyard of the prison. They gave him a loaf of bread each day from the bakers’ street until all the bread in the city was gone. So Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the prison.
Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words Jeremiah was speaking to all the people:
“This is what the Lord says: Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, famine, or plague. But whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live and save his life.
This is what the Lord says: This city will be handed over to the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.”

The officials said to the king, “This man must be put to death, because he is discouraging the fighting men who remain in this city and all the people by saying these things to them. This man does not want the welfare of this people, but their harm.”
King Zedekiah said, “Look, he is handed over to you, for the king cannot say anything against you.”

They took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah the king’s son, in the courtyard of the prison. They lowered Jeremiah into the cistern with a rope. There was no water in the cistern, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into the mud.
Ebed-melech the Cushite, a eunuch who was in the king’s palace, heard that they had thrown Jeremiah into the cistern. The king was sitting at the Benjamin Gate.
Ebed-melech went out from the king’s palace and spoke to the king.
My lord, these men have done wrong in everything they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they threw into the pit. Look, he is dying of hunger, because there is no bread in the city.
The king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, saying, “Take thirty men from here with you, and go and bring Jeremiah up from the cistern before he dies.”

Ebed-melech the Cushite took the men with him and entered the storeroom beneath the king’s palace. He took worn-out clothing and old rags from there and lowered them by a rope to Jeremiah in the cistern.
Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah, “Put the worn-out clothing and rags under your armpits, beneath the rope.” Jeremiah did so.
They pulled Jeremiah up with the rope and brought him out of the cistern. Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the prison.

King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet and had him brought to him, inside the three entrances of the Lord’s house. The king said to Jeremiah, “I am going to ask you something. Do not hide anything from me.”
Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “If I tell you, you will kill me. And if I give you advice, you will not listen to me.”
King Zedekiah secretly swore to Jeremiah in the house, saying, “As the Lord lives, who has given us life, I will not kill you or hand you over to the men who seek your life.”

Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: If you go out to the officials of the king of Babylon, you will save your life. This city will not be burned with fire, and you and your household will live.
But if you do not go out to the officials of the king of Babylon, this city will be handed over to the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire. You will not escape from their hands.”
King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “I am afraid of the Jews who have gone over to the Chaldeans. They might hand me over to them, and they will mock me.”
Jeremiah said, “They will not hand you over. Just obey the word of the Lord that I am telling you, so that things may go well for you and your life may be spared.
But if you refuse to go out, this is what the Lord has shown me:

All the women who remain in the palace of the king of Judah will go out to the officials of the king of Babylon. They will say, ‘The men who used to ask about your welfare have misled you and overcome you. Your feet have sunk into the mud, and they have turned back.’

They will bring out all your wives and children to the Chaldeans. You yourself will not escape from their hands, but will be handed over to the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned with fire.”
Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “Do not let anyone know about these words, so that you will not die.
If the officials hear that I have spoken with you and come to you and say, ‘Tell us what you said to the king and what the king said to you. Do not hide it from us, or we will kill you,’
He said to them, “I pleaded with the king not to send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, so that I would not die there.”
All the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him. He told them everything the king had instructed him to say. Then they left him alone, because the conversation had not been overheard.
Jeremiah remained in the prison courtyard until the day Jerusalem was captured.
In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with his entire army against Jerusalem and encamped against it.
In the eleventh year of King Zedekiah, in the fifth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city was breached.

All the officials of the king of Babylon came and took their seats at the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim the chief eunuch, Nergal-sharezer the chief magus, and all the other officials of the king of Babylon.

When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the fighting men saw them, they fled. They left the city at night by way of the king’s garden, through the gate between the walls, and went out along the road to the plain.

The Chaldean army pursued them and overtook Zedekiah on the plain of Jericho. His entire army scattered from him. They captured him and brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment on him.
The king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes at Riblah. The king of Babylon also slaughtered all the nobles of Judah.
He blinded Zedekiah and bound him in chains to take him to Babylon.
The Chaldeans burned down the king’s palace and the houses of the people, and tore down the wall all around Jerusalem.

Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, took captive the rest of the people who remained in the city, the people who had deserted to him, and the rest of the people who were left, and carried them away to Babylon.
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, left some of the poor people who had nothing in the land of Judah, and on that day he gave them vineyards and fields.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon gave Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, instructions concerning Jeremiah, saying to him:
“Take Jeremiah and look after him. Do him no harm, but do for him whatever he tells you.”
Then Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, Nebushazban the chief eunuch, Nergal-sharezer the chief magus, and all the officials of the king of Babylon sent.
They sent for Jeremiah and took him from the prison courtyard. They handed him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, to take him home. So he lived among the people.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah while he was confined in the courtyard of the guard:

“Go and tell Ebed-melech the Cushite: This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am bringing my words against this city to fulfillment, for disaster and not for good. They will take place before your eyes on that day.
But I will rescue you on that day, says the Lord, and you will not be handed over to the men you fear.
I will rescue you, and you will not fall by the sword. You will escape with your life because you have trusted in me, says the Lord.”

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, released him from Ramah, where he had taken him bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah who were being carried away to Babylon.
The captain of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him, ‘The LORD your God pronounced disaster against this place.’
“The Lord has brought it about and done as he said. Because you sinned against the Lord and did not obey him, this has happened to you.

But as for you, today I am freeing you from the chains on your hands. If you wish to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you. If you do not wish to come with me to Babylon, stay here. Look, the whole land is before you. Go wherever you think it is good and right to go.”

He said to him, “If you are staying, return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon appointed over the towns of Judah, and live among the people. Or go wherever you think best.” Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, gave him gifts for the journey and released him.
Jeremiah came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, at Mizpah, and lived with him among the people who remained in the land.

All the army commanders in those villages and the men with them heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land and had entrusted to him men, women, children, and some of the poor of the land who had not been taken captive to Babylon.

They came with their men to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai from Netophah, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite.

Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, swore an oath to them and to the men with them, saying, “Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Stay in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and things will go well for you.

As for me, I am staying at Mizpah to represent you before the Chaldeans who come to us. But you should gather grain, wine, oil, and summer fruit, put them in your storage containers, and live in the villages you have taken over.”

All the Jews in Edom, Moab, the land of the Ammonites, and all the other lands also heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of the Jews and had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, over them.
All the Jews returned from all the places where they had been scattered and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They gathered a very great abundance of wine and summer produce.
Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders in the villages came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
They said to him, “Do you not know that Baalis, king of the Ammonites, has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to kill you?” But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

Johanan son of Kareah said privately to Gedaliah at Mizpah, “Let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one will know. Otherwise he may kill you, and all the people of Judah who are gathering around you will be scattered, and the remnant of the Jews will perish.”
But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, “Do not do this, because you have spoken falsely about Ishmael.”

In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Ishmael, who was of royal descent, came with the king’s officials and twenty men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. They ate a meal together there at Mizpah.

Then Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the twenty men who had come with him rose up and struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword and killed him—the man whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
Ishmael also killed all the Jews who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, the Chaldeans who were found there, and the fighting men.
No one had heard about it, and on the second day after Gedaliah had been killed,

men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria—eighty men with their beards shaved, their clothes torn, and cuts on their bodies. They carried offerings and frankincense to bring into the house of the Lord.
Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he walked along. When he met them, he said to them, “Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.”
When they entered the town, Ishmael son of Nethaniah slaughtered them and threw them into the cistern, with the help of the men who were with him.
But ten men among them said to Ishmael, “Do not kill us, because we have stores of wheat, barley, oil, and honey in the field.” So he spared them and did not kill them along with their companions.

The cistern into which Ishmael threw all the bodies of the men he had killed along with Gedaliah was the one that Asa king of Judah had made because of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled that cistern with the dead.

Ishmael took captive all the rest of the people at Mizpah whom Nebuzaradan, the chief executioner, had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and set out to cross over to the Ammonites.
Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders with him heard about all the captives whom Ishmael son of Nethaniah had led away.
He took all the men and went to fight Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They found him by the great waters at Gibeon.
When all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders with him, they rejoiced.
All the people whom Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned back and came to Johanan son of Kareah.
But Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.

Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders with him took all the remaining people whom he had brought back from Ishmael son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, after Ishmael had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam. He took the fighting men, women, children, and eunuchs whom he had brought back from Gibeon.
And he went and stayed at the threshing floors of [?] near Bethlehem, intending to go into Egypt,
away from the Chaldeans, because they were afraid of them, since Ishmael son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed to govern the land of Judah.
Then all the army commanders, Johanan son of Kareah, Jaazaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people, from the youngest to the oldest, approached
and said to Jeremiah, “We ask you to pray for us before the LORD your God, because only a few of us remain out of many, as your own eyes can see.
May the LORD your God show us the way we should go and what we should do.”

Jeremiah the prophet said to them, “I have heard you. I will pray before the LORD your God as you have asked. Everything the LORD your God says in answer to you, I will tell you; I will not hide a word from you.”
They said to Jeremiah, “May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act according to the message that the LORD your God sends you to bring us.
Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you, so that things may go well for us when we obey the voice of the LORD our God.”
After ten days, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet.
He called Johanan son of Kareah, all the army commanders who were with him, and all the people, from the youngest to the oldest,
and said to them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says, to whom you sent me to present your request before him:
‘If you remain in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you, and I will stop bringing disaster upon you.
