Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you fear. Do not be afraid of him, says the LORD, because I am with you, says the LORD, to save you and rescue you from his hands.
I will grant you mercy, have compassion on you, and settle you in your own land.
But if you say, “We will not stay in this land,” refusing to obey the voice of the LORD your God,
and say, “No! We will go into the land of Egypt, where we will not see war or hear the sound of the trumpet or go hungry for bread, and we will settle there,”
then hear the word of the LORD, you remnant of Judah. This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: If you set your minds on entering Egypt and go there to live,
the sword you fear will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine you fear will pursue you into Egypt, and there you will die.
All the men who set their minds on entering Egypt to live there will die by sword, famine, and plague. They will have no survivor who escapes the disaster I am bringing upon them.’

For this is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Just as my anger and fury came to rest upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my fury will come to rest upon you when you enter Egypt. You will become an object of oaths, horror, cursing, and disgrace, and you will never see this place again.
The LORD has spoken concerning you, remnant of Judah: ‘Do not go into Egypt.’ Know that I have warned you today.
For you deceived yourselves when you sent me to the LORD your God and said, ‘Pray for us before the LORD our God, and tell us everything the LORD our God says to you, and we will do it.’
I have told you today, but you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God, and you have not done anything he sent me to tell you.
Now know that you will die by sword, famine, and plague in the place where you wanted to go and live.”
When Jeremiah had finished telling all the people all the words of the LORD their God, which the LORD their God had sent him to tell them,

Jaazaniah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the wicked men said to Jeremiah, “You are speaking falsely! The LORD our God did not send you to tell us, ‘Do not go into Egypt to live there.’
Rather, Baruch son of Neriah is stirring you up against us, to hand us over to the Chaldeans so that they may kill us and take us captive to Babylon.”
But Johanan son of Kareah, all the army commanders, and all the people did not obey the voice of the Lord by remaining in the land of Judah.
Johanan son of Kareah took all the army commanders and all the remnant who were left of the house of Judah,

the men, women, children, and royal household—all the people whom Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan—as well as Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
They went to the land of Egypt because they had not obeyed the voice of the Lord, and they came as far as Tahpanhes.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying:
Take large stones in your hand and bury them in the mortar of the brickwork at the entrance to Pharaoh’s palace in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah.

Tell them: This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am sending for my servant Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and bringing him here. He will set his throne above these stones that you have buried, and he will raise his weapons over them.
He will come and strike the land of Egypt, consigning those destined for death to death, those destined for captivity to captivity, and those destined for the sword to the sword.

He will set fire to the temples of the gods of Egypt, burn them, and take them captive. He will wrap the land around himself as a shepherd wraps himself in his cloak, and he will leave there in peace.
He will break the pillar of Beth-shemesh in the land of Egypt, and he will burn the temples of the Egyptian gods with fire.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, directing him to prophesy concerning all the Jews living in the land of Egypt, those living in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and the land of Pathros:
This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: You have seen all the disaster that I brought upon Jerusalem and all the towns of Judah. Today they lie in ruins, with no one living in them,
because of all the evil they did, provoking me to anger. They went and burned incense to other gods whom neither they nor their ancestors had known.
I sent all my servants the prophets to them, sending them early and repeatedly, saying, ‘Do not do this detestable thing that I hate.’
But they did not listen or incline their ears to turn from their evil deeds and stop burning incense to other gods.
My anger and fury descended, and fire took hold in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. They became a ruin and an object of horror, as they are today.

And now this is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Why are you doing such great evil to yourselves, cutting off from among you the men, women, young people, and infants of Judah, leaving yourselves no survivors?

You have provoked me to anger with the work of your hands and burned incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you have come to live, so that I will destroy you and you will become a curse and an object of scorn among all the nations of the earth.
Have you forgotten the evil of your ancestors, the evil of the kings of Judah, and the evil of their wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem?
To this day they have not purified themselves. They have not feared me or served me, nor have they followed my law and my covenant, which I gave to them and their ancestors.
Therefore this is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am setting my face against you to bring disaster and to destroy the whole house of Judah.

I will shatter the remnant of Judah who have set their faces toward entering Egypt to live there. They will all perish in the land of Egypt and die by sword, famine, and plague. They will become an object of cursing and horror, a curse and an object of scorn.
I will punish those living in the land of Egypt as I punished Jerusalem, with sword, famine, and plague.

Among the remnant of Judah who enter the land of Egypt to live there, none will escape or survive to return to the land of Judah, where they themselves hope to return. They will not return, except for a few.

Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, and all the women standing there—a large assembly—and all the people living in the land of Egypt and in Pathros answered Jeremiah and said to him:
As for the word you have spoken to us in the name of the Lord, we will not listen to you.

But we will carry out every word that has come from our mouths: we will burn incense in worship of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our officials did in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. Then we had plenty of bread, things went well for us, and we saw no disaster.
But ever since we stopped burning incense in worship of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been perishing by sword and famine.

All the women answered, saying, “When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, was it without our husbands that we made cakes for her and poured out drink offerings to her?”
Jeremiah said to all the people—to the men, the women, and all the people who had spoken these words to him:

That fragrant incense which you offered in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem—you, your ancestors, your kings, your officials, and the people of the land—the LORD remembered it, and it came to his mind.

The Lord could no longer forgive you because of your evil deeds and the abominations you committed. Your land became an object of horror, a curse, and a desolate place without inhabitants, as it is today.
Because you burned incense and sinned against the Lord, did not obey the Lord’s voice, and did not follow his law, his covenant, and his testimonies, this disaster has overtaken you, as it has today.
Jeremiah said to all the people, both men and women, “Hear the word of the Lord, all you people of Judah in the land of Egypt.

This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives have spoken with your mouths and are carrying it out with your hands. You said, ‘We will fulfill the vows we made to burn incense in worship of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.’ You have confirmed your oaths and carried out your vows.

Therefore hear the word of the Lord, all you people of Judah living in the land of Egypt: Look, I have sworn by my great name, says the Lord, that my name will no longer be on the lips of the people of Judah anywhere in the land of Egypt. They will no longer say, ‘As the Lord God lives.’
For I am hastening disaster upon them, says the Lord. All the men of Judah in the land of Egypt will perish by sword, famine, and plague, until I have made an end of them.

Those who escape the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, few in number. Then the entire remnant of Judah who went to settle in the land of Egypt will know whose word stands—mine or theirs.
This will be the sign to you, says the Lord, that I will punish you in this place, so that you may know that my words concerning disaster against you will stand.

This is what the Lord says: Look, I am handing Pharaoh the Lame, king of Egypt, over to his enemies and to those who seek his life, just as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.
The word Jeremiah spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when he wrote these words in a scroll at Jeremiah’s dictation, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says concerning you, Baruch:
You said, “Woe to me, for the Lord has added sorrow to my pain! I am worn out with my groaning and have found no rest.”
Say this to him: This is what the Lord says: Look, what I built I am tearing down, and what I planted I am uprooting. I am laying waste the whole land.

But you have sought great things for yourself. Do not seek things beyond you, for look, I am bringing disaster upon all flesh, says the Lord. But I will grant that you escape with your life wherever you go.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he should prophesy concerning the nations.

Concerning the Egyptians and the army of Pharaoh the Lame, king of Egypt, which was encamped by the Euphrates River at Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Take up weapons and shields, and advance to battle.
Muster the horses! Mount the horsemen! Put on helmets! Polish the spears! Put on armor!
For I have seen them shattered and turning back. Their warriors have been struck down and have fled without looking back, because they were surrounded on every side, says the Lord.
The swift will not flee, nor will the mightiest of warriors escape. Beside the Euphrates River they have all stumbled and fallen.
Who is this rising like the river, whose waters surge like rivers?
The king of Egypt rises like the river, and his waters surge like rivers. He says, “I will rise and cover the earth; I will destroy the city and its inhabitants.”
Mount the horses! Glory in the chariots! Let the warriors go out—the Cushites and the people of Put who carry shields, and the Lydians who know how to shoot with the bow.

That day will belong to the Lord Almighty, a day of vengeance, when he takes vengeance on his enemies. The sword will devour and be satisfied, and drink its fill of their blood, because the Lord Almighty will bring slaughter in the northern land, by the Euphrates River.
Go up to Gilead and get medicinal herbs, virgin daughter of Egypt. In vain you have multiplied your remedies; no help has come to you.
The nations have heard of your disgrace, and your wailing has filled the earth, because one man has stumbled against another, and both have fallen by the sword.
The message that the Lord spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon would come and devastate the land of Egypt.
Declare it in Egypt, proclaim it in Migdol, and proclaim it in Memphis and Tahpanhes. Say, “Prepare yourselves and stand ready, because the sword has devoured those around you.”
Why were your mighty men swept away? They fell and did not stand, because the Lord overthrew them.
Many of them were overthrown; one man fell over another. They said, “Come, let us return to our people and to the land where we were born, away from the devastating sword.”
There they called Pharaoh, the lame king of Egypt, “An uproar who lets the appointed times pass.”
“As I live,” says the King, whose name is the Lord of Hosts, “Pharaoh will surely fall like a broken piece of a mountain, and like Carmel into the sea.”
Pack your belongings for captivity, virgin daughter of Egypt, because Memphis will become a ruin and lie desolate, without anyone living there.
Egypt is a beautiful, adorned heifer. An army from the north has come against her.
Her hired soldiers within her are like fattened calves. They too turned and fled together; they did not stand, because the day of their ruin had come upon them, the time of their punishment.
The sound of the army is like a snake slithering, because they will march against the army and come against her with axes, like woodcutters.
“Cut down her forests,” says the Lord, “for there is no end to them. They are more numerous than locusts and cannot be counted.”
The daughter of Egypt has been put to shame and handed over to the people of the north.

The Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says, “Look, I am bringing punishment upon Amon of the waters, upon Pharaoh, upon Egypt, upon her gods, upon her army, upon her kings, upon Pharaoh, and upon everyone who trusts in him.”
“I will hand them over to their enemies and to those who seek their lives—to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his servants. Afterward she will be inhabited as in former days,” says the Lord.

“But you, my servant Jacob, do not be afraid,” says the Lord. “Do not be dismayed, Israel, for I am saving you from far away, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be at peace, quiet and at rest, with no one to frighten him.

“You, my servant Jacob, do not be afraid,” says the Lord, “because I am with you. I will make an end of all the nations among whom I scattered you, but I will not make an end of you. I will discipline you justly, and I will certainly not leave you unpunished.”
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, telling him to prophesy against the Philistines before Pharaoh struck Gaza.

This is what the Lord says: “Look, I am bringing young men from the north. They will be like an overflowing torrent, sweeping away the land and everything in it, the town and its inhabitants. People will groan, and all the inhabitants of the land will wail.
“At the sound of the pounding hooves of his mighty horses, at the shaking of his chariots and the sound of his wheels, fathers did not turn back to their children, because their hands had grown weak.

“Look, the day is coming to plunder all the Philistines and to destroy Tyre and Sidon and everyone left to help them, because the Lord is devastating the Philistines, the remnant from the islands of the Cappadocians.
“A blow has fallen on Gaza. Ashkelon has been shattered, along with everyone left in their settlements.”
O sword of the Lord, how long will you remain restless and not rest from devastating? Withdraw into your sheath! Withdraw and be still!
How can it be still when the Lord has commanded it against Ashkelon and the seacoasts? There he has given it authority.
Concerning Moab.
This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: “Woe to Nebo, for it has been plundered! Kiriathaim has been put to shame and humiliated. Her stronghold has been put to shame and scattered.
“There is no longer any praise for Moab. In Heshbon they plotted evil against her and said, ‘Come, let us destroy her as a nation.’ Even if you remain completely silent, the sword will pursue you.”
A sound of wailing from Horonaim: plunder and great destruction!
Moab is shattered; its poor have raised a wail.
They will climb the ascent of Luhith weeping, and on the descent of Horonaim they will raise cries of distress and destruction. Listen!
Flee and save your lives! Be like a root in the wilderness.
Because you trusted in your strongholds and your treasures, you too will be captured. Chemosh will go into captivity, together with his priests and his officials.
The plunderer will come against all your towns, and they will not escape. The valley will perish and the plain will be devastated, just as the Lord has said.
Give Moab a crown, for it is being utterly devastated. All its towns will become ruins, with no one living in them.
Cursed is anyone who does the Lord’s work deceitfully, and cursed is anyone who keeps his sword from bloodshed.

The Moabites have been at ease since their youth, resting undisturbed on their sediment. They have not been poured from one vessel into another, nor have they gone into captivity. Therefore their taste remains in them, and their scent has not faded.
Therefore, look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will send plunderers against them. They will plunder them, empty their vessels, and smash their jars.
Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, just as the Israelites were ashamed of Bethel, in which they trusted.
How can you say, ‘We are warriors, mighty men in battle’?
Moab has been plundered, and the attacker has advanced against its towns. Its chosen warriors have been handed over to slaughter, says the King, whose name is the Lord, the mighty God.
Moab’s destruction is near, and its disaster is coming very quickly.
Be distressed and tremble, all you who surround it. All you who know its name, say, ‘How the mighty staff has been broken, the glorious rod!’
Come down from glory and sit in disgrace, you who inhabit the daughter of Dibon [?], for Moab’s plunderer has advanced against you and destroyed your fortresses.
Stand beside the roads and watch, you who inhabit Aroer [?]. Ask the one fleeing and the one escaping; say, ‘What has happened?’
Moab is ashamed because it has been shattered. Wail and cry out in Arnon, because Moab has been shattered.
Judgment has come upon the land of the plateau, upon Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath,
upon Dibon [?], Nebo, and Beth-diblathaim,
upon Kiriathaim, Beth-gamul, and Beth-meon,
upon Kerioth, Bozrah, and all the towns of the land of Moab, far and near.
Moab’s horn has been cut off, and its arm has been broken, says the Lord.
Make him sick, because he has exalted himself against the Lord. Moab will wallow in his vomit, and he too will become a laughingstock.
Was not Israel a laughingstock to you? Was he found among thieves when you were waging war against him?
Leave the towns and settle among the cliffs, inhabitants of Moab. Be like a dove that nests on a rocky ledge.
We have heard of the leaders of Moab, who are very proud—their pride, their arrogance, and the haughtiness of their hearts.
“I know,” says the Lord, “that their deeds were not right, and his diviners did not declare this about him.”
Therefore wail over Moab, and cry out from everywhere over all Moab. Let them speak of disaster for the people who live in it.

More than the weeping for Jazer, I will weep for you, vine of Sibmah. Your branches crossed the sea and reached as far as the sea of Jazer, for a plunderer has fallen upon your harvest and your grape gathering.
Joy and gladness will pass away from the fertile countryside and from the land of Moab. Wine will cease from the winepress. The treaders will not tread, nor will they sing out or say, “Hey! Hey!”

From the wailing of Heshbon as far as Elealeh and Jahaz, they have raised their voices; from Zoar as far as Horonaim and as far as the fortress of Alas, Eglath-shelishiyah, for the waters of Nimrim will disappear.
“I will put an end in Moab,” says the Lord, “to anyone who offers a burnt offering and burns incense to his god.”
Therefore my heart will sound like a harp over Moab, because they did evil and perished.
For their heads are shaved and their beards are cut off. There are cuts on all their hands, and sackcloth around their waists.
On every rooftop in Moab and in all its streets there is mourning, because I have broken Moab like a vessel for which there is no use, says the Lord.
How they have been shattered and have wailed! How Moab has turned his back in shame! Moab will become an object of ridicule and ruin to everyone around him.
This is what the Lord says: Look, he will rise and soar like an eagle and spread his wings over Moab.
Kerioth has been captured, and the fortress has been conquered. On that day the hearts of Moab’s warriors will be like the heart of a woman suffering the pains of childbirth.
Moab will cease to be a people, because he exalted himself against the Lord.
Terror, a pit, and a trap await you, inhabitant of Moab, says the Lord.

Whoever flees from the sound of terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in the trap. For I am bringing these things upon Moab in the year of their punishment, says the Lord.
For fire has gone out from Heshbon, and a flame from the fortress of Sihon. It will consume the face of Moab and the leaders of the tumultuous people.
Woe to you, Moab! You have perished, people of Chemosh, for your sons and daughters have been scattered into captivity.
“But I will restore Moab’s captives in the last days,” says the Lord. Here ends the judgment of Moab.
Concerning the Ammonites.
This is what the Lord says: Does Israel have no sons? Does he have no heirs? Why, then, has Milcom taken possession of Gad, and why have his people settled in its towns?

Therefore, look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make the sound of battle heard against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It will become a ruined mound, and its villages will be burned with fire. Israel will take possession of those who took possession of him, says the Lord.

Wail, Heshbon, for Ai has been destroyed! Lament, villages of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth, mourn, and cut yourselves with sharp instruments, for Milcom will go into captivity, together with his priests and his officials, says the Lord.
Why do you boast in your valleys and trust in your ravines, beloved daughter, who trusts in her treasures and says, “Who will come against me?”
Look, I am bringing terror upon you from all around you, says the mighty Lord. I will scatter them, each in his own direction, and there will be no one to gather those who have been scattered.
But afterward I will restore the captives of the Ammonites, says the Lord.
This is what the Lord Almighty says: Is there no longer any wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the discerning? Has their wisdom been taken away?
Flee, turn back, and hide deep away, inhabitants of Dedan [?], for I have brought Esau’s destruction upon him, the time of his punishment, says the Lord.
If grape gatherers came against you, would they not leave gleanings? And if thieves came at night, they would destroy as much as they wished.
For I have searched Esau and uncovered his hiding places. He hid himself and was not found. His descendants, his brothers, and his neighbors were scattered, and they are no more.
Leave your orphans; I will keep them alive. Let your widows trust in me.

For this is what the Lord says: Look, those who were not required to drink the cup have drunk it. Did you think you would escape punishment? You will not escape punishment; you too will drink the cup.
For I have sworn by myself, says the Lord, that Bozrah will become an object of horror, a ruin, a disgrace, and a curse. All her towns will become ruins forever.
I have heard news from the Lord, and a messenger has been sent to the nations: Rise up! Let us go up against her for battle!
For look, I have made you small among the nations and despised among humankind.

Your wickedness has deceived you, along with the pride of your heart—you who live in the clefts of the rock and occupy the heights of the hill, saying in your heart, ‘Who will bring me down to the ground?’ Even if you place your nest among the stars, even if you raise your nest high like an eagle, I will bring you down from there, says the Lord.
Edom will become a ruin. Everyone who passes by her will be appalled and hiss at all her wounds.
She will be overthrown as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, says the Lord. No one will live there, and no human being will dwell there.

Look, like a lion he will come up from the thickets of the Jordan against the enduring pasture. In a moment I will drive them away from it, and I will appoint troops over it. For who is like me? Who can summon me to account? What shepherd can stand before me?

Therefore hear the Lord’s plan that he has devised against Edom, and the purpose he has formed against the inhabitants of Teman: The smallest of the flock will drag them away, and they will lay waste their pasture around them.
At the sound of their downfall the earth trembled. Her wailing—its sound was heard from the Red Sea.
Look, he will rise and soar like an eagle and spread his wings over Bozrah. On that day the hearts of Edom’s warriors will be like the heart of a woman suffering the pains of childbirth.
Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, for they have heard bad news and are shattered. She is afraid at the sea and cannot find rest.
Damascus has grown weak and turned to flee. Trembling has seized her; distress and pains have gripped her like a woman giving birth.
How has the celebrated city, the joyful city, not been abandoned?
Therefore her troops will fall in her streets, and all her warriors will be silenced on that day, says the Lord Almighty.
I will release fire in the streets of Damascus, and it will consume the fortresses of Ben-hadad.
This is what the Lord says: Rise up, advance against Kedar, and plunder the people of the east.
They will take their tents and their flocks. They will carry off their tent curtains, all their possessions, and their camels. They will cry out against them, ‘Attackers on every side!’
Flee, wander away, and hide deep away, inhabitants of Hazor, says the Lord. For Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has taken counsel against them and devised a plan against them, saying:
Rise up, advance against a prosperous nation living at ease, says the Lord, a nation with neither gates nor bars, living alone.

Their camels will become plunder, and their abundant livestock will become spoil. I will scatter them to every wind among those who clip the edges of their hair. From every side I will bring their destruction, says the Lord.
Hazor will become a dwelling place for jackals, a ruin forever. No one will live there, and no human being will dwell there.
The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet, for him to prophesy against Elam, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah.
This is what the Lord Almighty says: Look, I am breaking the bow of Elam, the chief source of their strength.
I will bring four winds against Elam from the four corners of heaven, and I will scatter them to all these winds. There will be no nation where the scattered people of Elam are not found.

“I will shatter Elam before their enemies and before those who seek their lives. I will bring disaster upon them, my fierce anger,” says the Lord. “I will send the sword among them until I have destroyed them.”
I will set my throne in Elam and destroy kings and rulers from there, says the Lord.
But in the last days I will bring back the captives of Elam, says the Lord.
The word that the Lord spoke against Babylon and against the land of the Chaldeans through Jeremiah the prophet.

Declare it among the nations and announce it. Raise a banner; announce it and do not hide it. Say: Babylon has been captured! Bel has fallen, and Merodach has been put to shame. Her idols have been disgraced, and her carved images have been broken.
For a nation has come up against her from the north. It will make her land a wasteland, with no one living in it. People and animals alike have fled and gone away.
In those days and at that time, says the Lord, the people of Israel and the people of Judah will come together, walking and weeping, seeking the Lord their God.
They will ask about the roads to Zion, with their faces turned toward it: Come, let us join ourselves to the Lord in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.
My people were like lost sheep. Their shepherds led them astray and scattered them on the mountains. They went from mountain to hill and forgot their resting place.

Everyone who found them devoured them, and their enemies say: We will not spare them, because they sinned against the Lord and against his righteous dwelling place. The Lord is the hope of their ancestors.
Flee from within Babylon! Leave the land of the Chaldeans, and be like male goats leading the flock.

For look, I am stirring up and bringing against Babylon assemblies of many nations from the northern land. They will draw up their battle lines against her, and from there she will be captured. Their arrows are like a successful warrior who does not return empty-handed.
The land of the Chaldeans will become plunder, and all who plunder her will have their fill, says the Lord.
Because you rejoice and celebrate, you, the chief of my inheritance [?], and leap like fattened calves and dance like rams of the flock.
Your mother is deeply ashamed, and the one who gave birth to you is disgraced. Look, she is the last of the nations, like a wilderness, ruined and desolate.
Because of the Lord’s anger, she will not be inhabited but will be entirely desolate. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be appalled and hiss at all her wounds.
Draw up your ranks against Babylon, all you who know how to shoot a bow. Shoot at her; do not spare your arrows, because she has sinned against the Lord.

Raise a shout against her from every side! She has surrendered. Her foundations have fallen, and her walls have been overthrown. For this is the Lord's vengeance. Take vengeance on her; do to her as she has done.

Destroy the sower from Babylon, and the one who holds the sickle at harvesttime. Because of the sword that brings suffering, everyone will turn back to their own people, and everyone will flee to their own land.
Israel is a wandering sheep; lions have driven them astray. First the king of Assyria devoured him, and now this last one, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, has overpowered him.
Therefore this is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Look, I will punish the king of Babylon and his land, just as I punished the king of Assyria.
I will bring Israel back to their pasture, and they will graze in Carmel and Bashan, on the mountain of Ephraim and in Gilead, and they will be satisfied.

In those days and at that time, says the Lord Almighty, Israel's guilt will be sought, but it will not exist; Judah's sin will be sought, but it will not be found. For I will forgive the remnant who remain among them.
Go up against the rebellious land! Go up against her and against her inhabitants! Awake, sword, and destroy them, says the Lord, and do as I commanded you.
The sound of someone calling in the land, and great destruction!
How the mighty power of the whole earth has been broken and swept away! How Babylon has become an object of astonishment among the nations!
You have been tripped up, Babylon, and you have also been captured. You did not know that you had risen against the Lord.
The Lord has opened his storehouse and brought out the weapons of his anger, for the Lord God Almighty has work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
Come against her from every side! Open her gates! Ransack her like a naked woman and destroy her. Leave nothing of her remaining.
Destroy her, and let all her bulls be handed over for slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has arrived, the time of their punishment!
The sound of those fleeing and escaping from the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of the Lord our God, vengeance for his temple.

Summon many against Babylon, everyone who knows how to shoot a bow. Shoot at her from every side, and leave her no survivors. Repay her as she deserves; do to her everything she has done, because she has acted arrogantly against the Lord, against the Holy One of Israel.
Therefore her troops will fall within her, and all her fighting men will be silenced on that day.
Look, I am against you, arrogant one, says the Lord God Almighty, for your day has arrived, the time of your punishment.
The arrogant one will stumble and fall, and no one will raise him up. I will set fire to his towns, and it will consume everything around him.
This is what the Lord of Hosts says: The people of Israel and the people of Judah are oppressed together. All who took them captive hold them fast and refuse to let them go.
Their Redeemer is strong; the Lord Almighty is his name. He will certainly plead their case, bringing rest to the earth and troubling all the inhabitants of the world.
A sword against the Chaldeans, says the Lord, and against all the inhabitants of Babylon, against her officials and against her wise men!
A sword against her diviners, and they will become confused! A sword against her warriors, and they will be shattered!
A sword against her horses, against her chariots, and against all the foreigners living within her, and they will become like women! A sword against her treasures, and they will be plundered!
A sword against her waters, and they will dry up! For it is a land of carved images, and they boast in idols.
Therefore sirens will dwell there, and ostriches will settle there. She will never again be inhabited or settled, from generation to generation.
She will be like Sodom and Gomorrah, which God overthrew along with their inhabitants. No one will live there, and no human being will settle there.
Look, a people is coming from the north, a great people, and many kings will be stirred up from the ends of the earth.
They are armed with bows and spears. They are cruel and have no mercy. Their sound is like the raging sea. They ride horses and are prepared like warriors for battle against you, daughter Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard the report about them, and his hands have gone limp. Distress has seized him, and pains like those of a woman giving birth.

Look, he will come up like a lion from the swollen Jordan against a secure fold. For I will quickly drive them away from her, and I will put raiding bands in charge of her. For who is like me? Who can challenge me? What shepherd can stand against me?

Therefore hear the Lord's plan that he has devised against Babylon, and his purpose that he has formed against the land of the Chaldeans: the smallest of the flock will drag them away, and their folds will be devastated because of them.
At the news that Babylon had been captured, the earth shook; her wailing was heard among the nations.
This is what the Lord God Almighty says: Look, I am stirring up a hard heart and a destroying wind against Babylon and against her inhabitants.
I will send plunderers against Babylon. They will plunder her and trample her land, and they will gather against her from every side on the day of disaster.
Let the archer not stop, and let the warrior not take off his armor. Do not spare her raiding bands; destroy her entire army.
The slain will fall in the land of the Chaldeans, and the wounded in her streets.
For Israel and Judah have not been left widowed by their God, by the Lord Almighty, their God; for their land is filled with wrongdoing before the Holy One of Israel.
Flee from Babylon, and let everyone save his own life! Do not perish because of her sins, for this is the time of the Lord’s vengeance. He is repaying her according to her deeds.
Babylon was a golden cup in the Lord’s hand, making the whole earth drunk. All the nations drank her wine and went mad.
Suddenly Babylon has fallen and been plundered. Wail over her! Bring medicines for her wounds; perhaps she will be healed.
We treated Babylon, but she was not healed. Let us abandon her and go, each to his own land, for her judgment has reached heaven and risen to the clouds.
The Lord has brought about our vindication. Come, let us recount in Zion the deeds of the Lord our God.

Gather the shields! Fill up with arrows! The Lord has stirred up the spirit of the king of Media, because his purpose is to destroy Babylon. For this is the Lord’s vengeance, retribution for his temple.
Raise a banner against Babylon’s walls! Set up a watch and drown her in water, for the Lord has carried out what he planned against Babylon.
You who lived beside abundant waters, your treasures are many. Your end has come, and your wound has grown severe.
The mighty Lord has sworn by himself: I will fill you with people like locusts, and they will raise a cry over you, saying, ‘Ha! Ha!’
The Lord made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
He makes the waters roar in heaven. He brings clouds up from the ends of the earth, makes lightning for the rain, and brings winds out of his storehouses.
Everyone is foolish and without knowledge. All metalworkers are put to shame by the carved images they have made, for they have cast falsehood, and there is no breath in them.
They are nothing, works of foolishness. When the time comes for them to be punished, they will perish.
Jacob’s portion is not like these. Rather, the one who created everything is their portion and the tribe of their inheritance. The mighty Lord is his name.
Prepare weapons of war for me! With you I will scatter nations, and with you I will destroy kingdoms.
With you I will scatter horses and their riders, and with you I will scatter chariots and those who ride in them.
With you I will scatter men and women, with you I will scatter the old and the young, and with you I will scatter young men and young women.
With you I will scatter the shepherd and his flock, with you I will scatter the farmer and his team of oxen, and with you I will scatter rulers and governors.
I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea for all the evil they did in Zion before your eyes, says the Lord.
Look, I am against you, destructive mountain, says the Lord, you who destroyed the whole earth. I will raise my hand against you, roll you down from the rock, and make you a burned mountain.
They will not take from you a stone for a corner or a stone for a foundation. Instead, you will be a ruin forever, says the Lord.

Raise a banner in the land! Sound the trumpet among the nations! Prepare nations against her! Summon against her the kingdoms of [?], Armenia, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a destroyer against her! Bring up horses like locusts!
Prepare nations against her—the king of Media, his nobles, and all his governors.
The earth will quake and tremble, because the Lord’s plan against Babylon has been established: to lay waste the land of Babylon, leaving it without an inhabitant.
Babylon’s warriors have stopped fighting with the inhabitants of the fortresses. Their might has been broken, and they have become like women. Uproot her dwellings! Break her gates!
Runner will run to meet runner, and messenger to meet messenger, to tell the king of Babylon that his city has been captured from every side.
Its crossings have been seized, its marshes have been burned with fire, and all its warriors are terrified.
For this is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: “The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor when the time has come to tread it. In a little while her harvest will come.”

Jerusalem said, “Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, has devoured me and plundered me. He has left me like an empty vessel. He has swallowed me like a dragon, filled his belly with my delicacies, and driven me away.”
“My plunder and my possessions were carried off to Babylon, and my blood is on the inhabitants of Chaldea,” Jerusalem will say.
Therefore this is what the Lord says: “Look, I will plead your case and take vengeance for you. I will dry up Babylon’s sea and make its springs run dry.
Babylon will become a ruin, a dwelling for jackals, an object of horror and hissing, with no one living in it.
They will roar like lions and growl like lion cubs.
In anger I will prepare their feast and make them drunk. They will be shattered and sleep forever, never to wake,” says the Lord.
“I will hand them over like fattened animals for killing, like rams and young goats for slaughter.
How [?], the praise of the whole earth, has been captured! How Babylon has become an object of horror among the nations!
The sea has risen over Babylon, and it has been covered by its many waves.
Its towns have become an object of horror, like a ruined and desolate land. No one will live in them, and no human being will dwell in them.
I will punish Bel in Babylon and bring what he has swallowed out of his mouth. The nations will no longer fear him, and Babylon’s broad walls will fall.
Come out of it, my people! Each of you, save your life from the fierce anger of the Lord.

Do not let your hearts break or be afraid because of the report heard in the land. A report will come in one year, and after that year another report. There will be violence in the land, and ruler will rise against ruler.
Therefore, look, the days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will punish Babylon’s carved idols. Its whole land will perish, and all its slain will fall within it.
Heaven and earth and everything in them will rejoice over Babylon, because plunderers will come against it from the north,” says the Lord.
“In Babylon too the slain of Israel will fall, and because of Babylon the slain will fall throughout the earth.
You who have escaped the sword, go! Do not stand still. Remember the Lord from far away, and let Jerusalem come to mind.” And those of the house of Israel will say:
“We are deeply ashamed, because we have heard insults. Shame has covered our faces, because foreigners have entered the Lord’s sanctuary.”
“Therefore, look, the days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will punish Babylon and its carved idols, and throughout its land its slain will fall.
Even if Babylon rises to heaven and sets its stronghold on high, plunderers will come against it from me,” says the Lord.
The sound of wailing comes from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans.
For the Lord has plundered Babylon and destroyed its people and animals—a mighty sound, like abundant waters whose roar resounds.
For plunderers have come against Babylon, its mighty warriors have been captured, and their bows have been broken. For the Lord is a God of repayment; he will surely repay them.
“I will make her leaders, her wise men, her nobles, her rulers, and her warriors drunk. They will sleep forever and will not awaken,” says the King, whose name is the Lord Almighty.

This is what the mighty Lord says: “Babylon’s broad walls will be utterly uprooted, and its high gates will be burned with fire. Peoples will labor in vain, and nations will wear themselves out in the fire.”

The message that the prophet Jeremiah entrusted to Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went with King Zedekiah of Judah to Babylon in the eleventh year of his reign. Seraiah was the camp commander.
Jeremiah wrote in one scroll all the disaster that was coming upon Babylon—all these words written against Babylon.
Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you enter Babylon, read and examine all these words.”
And he said, “LORD, you have spoken against this place, to destroy it so that no one will live in it, neither human nor animal, because it will be a wasteland forever.”
When you have finished reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates.
Here end the words of Jeremiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
He did what was evil in the LORD’s sight, just as Jehoiakim had done.
Because of these things, the LORD’s anger was against Jerusalem and Judah until he cast them out of his presence. And King Zedekiah rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.

In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in that month, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came against Jerusalem with his entire army. They encamped against it and built siegeworks all around it.
The city remained under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
In the seventh month, on the ninth day of the month, the famine became severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

The city wall was breached, and all the fighting men fled, leaving the city at night by the gate between the walls beside the king’s garden. The Chaldeans were surrounding the city, and they went along the road toward the plain.
The Chaldean army pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah on the plain of Jericho. His entire army scattered away from him.
They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, and he pronounced judgment on him.
The king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, and he put all the nobles of Judah to the sword at Riblah.
He blinded Zedekiah and bound him with chains. The king of Babylon took him to Babylon and put him in prison until the day he died.

In the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month—it was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon—Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, came and stood before the king of Babylon in Jerusalem.
He burned the LORD’s house, the palace of the king of Judah, and all the houses of Jerusalem. They burned down all the houses of the leading men.
The entire Chaldean army that was with the commander of the guard demolished all the walls around Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan took into exile some of the poor people, the rest of the people who remained in the city, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the population.
But Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, left some of the poor people of the land to tend the vineyards and work the land.
The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars, the basins, and the bronze Sea in the LORD’s house. They took all their bronze and carried it to Babylon.
They also took the pots, shovels, [?], basins, spoons, and all the bronze utensils used in the service.
The commander of the guard also took the [?], censers, [?], pots, snuffers, lampstands, spoons, and bowls made of gold and silver.
The two bronze pillars, the one Sea, and the twelve bronze bulls beneath the sides of the Sea were what King Solomon had made for the LORD’s house. The bronze of these articles was beyond weighing.
As for those two pillars, one of them was eighteen cubits high, and a cord twelve cubits long went around it. It was four fingerbreadths thick and hollow inside.

There was a bronze capital on it, and the height of one capital was five cubits. There were meshwork and pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze. The other pillar and its pomegranates were like these.
There were ninety-six pomegranates; there were one hundred pomegranates in all on the latticework all around.
The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three gatekeepers.

From the city he took one eunuch who was in charge of the fighting men, seven prominent men who appeared before the king and who remained in the city, the scribe and the commander of the army of the people of the land, and sixty men from the people of the land who were found inside the city.
Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath.
The king of Babylon struck them down and killed them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was taken captive from its land.
These are the people whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took captive: in the seventh year of his reign, 3,023 Jews;
and in the eighteenth year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, he took 832 people captive from Jerusalem;
and in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took 745 Jewish people captive. There were 4,600 people in all.

In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year of his reign, raised the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of prison.
He spoke kindly to him and placed his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes and ate regularly in the king’s presence all the days of his life.
His allowance was provided regularly by the king of Babylon every day until the day he died, all the days of his life.
